# Naima

> A project tracker whose items are files in your git repository, under
> naima-tracker/, for software built by people and AI agents. It runs from a
> clone of Naima's dist branch, locked to one commit; Deno runs it.

## Install it in a repository

Work from the root of the git repository to track (`git rev-parse --show-toplevel`).

1. Run the installer for this system:
   - macOS, Linux: `curl -fsSL https://vincenzoml.github.io/naima/install.sh | sh`
   - Windows (PowerShell): `irm https://vincenzoml.github.io/naima/install.ps1 | iex`

   It needs git. It installs Deno with Deno's official installer when Deno is
   missing (set `NAIMA_NO_DENO_INSTALL=1` to be told how instead). It clones
   https://github.com/vincenzoml/naima.git, branch `dist`, into
   `naima-tracker/naima/` (ignored by git), runs `naima init`, which writes
   `naima-tracker/` and nothing else, and runs `naima check`. Run again, it
   only checks. It refuses, in one line, outside a git repository.

2. Check it: `deno run -A naima-tracker/naima/naima.ts check` must end with
   `all invariants hold`.

3. Commit it: `git add naima-tracker && git commit -m "Track this project with Naima"`.

4. Learn the workflow: read `naima-tracker/naima/skills/naima/SKILL.md` and
   follow it; every tracker change goes through the CLI. In it, `naima` means
   `deno run -A naima-tracker/naima/naima.ts`.

## By hand, without the installer

```sh
git clone --branch dist https://github.com/vincenzoml/naima.git naima-tracker/naima
deno run -A naima-tracker/naima/naima.ts init
deno run -A naima-tracker/naima/naima.ts check
```
